about: Tool definitions for the Kaam Ki Baat voice agent, as configured on the live agent on 30 October 2026. Platform-neutral: create one HTTP tool per entry on your voice platform. Tool and parameter names must match exactly, because the prompt calls them by name. Paste each description in full: the model reads it when deciding whether to call the tool. In url, headers and body, replace {API_BASE}, {API_KEY} and {ACTING_ORG_ID} with your registry instance values; {name} in a body is filled from the parameter of that name. GET tools send their parameters as query parameters. hold_message: whether the platform plays a short hold line while the call runs.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Get the caller's profile from the database by phone number.

phone_number.description: The caller's mobile number with the 91 country-code prefix and NO plus sign, e.g. 919876543210

tools.name: create_profile
tools.description: Create a seeker profile for a NEW caller ONLY if get_profile returned no profile. Returns {user_id, items[]}: items[0].item_id is the new profile_id.

age.description: Caller's age in years, e.g. 28 Send as a NUMBER, not a string.

role.description: The job role/trade the caller wants, e.g. Electrician

phone.description: The caller's number in the SAME form you sent to get_profile: 12 digits beginning with 91, digits only, no plus sign - e.g. 919876543210. Build it by FORMAT, not by adding: if ${contact_phone} is already 12 digits starting with 91 (outbound calls), send it UNCHANGED and never add another 91; if it is 10 digits (inbound calls), put 91 in front. A number starting 9191 is always wrong - the backend finds users by phone, so a doubled prefix silently creates a separate phantom user.

gender.description: The caller's gender. MUST be exactly one of: "Male", "Female", "Other", "Don't want to share". Map the caller's answer to one of these; never send any other string (the API rejects off-list values).

itiTrade.description: Only if educationCategory='ITI'. The enum is a 150+ NSQF trade list; for voice, set 'Other' and put the spoken trade in itiTradeOther, UNLESS the spoken trade is an obvious exact match (e.g. 'Electrician', 'Fitter', 'Welder (NSQF)', 'Data Entry Operator (NSQF)').

location.description: Caller's location as City, State, India REQUIRED: without a location the created profile stays 'draft' and cannot be applied to (apply fails PROFILE_NOT_LIVE).

itiInstitute.description: Free text; the ITI or Polytechnic college/institute name the caller studied at.

itiTradeOther.description: Free text; the ITI trade as the caller said it. Used when itiTrade='Other'.

workExperience.description: The caller's work-experience category. MUST be exactly one of: "Fresher", "Worked before", "Returning after a break". Map the caller's spoken answer to one of these three; never send any other string (the API rejects off-list values).

otherHelpNeeded.description: Other help the caller needs to get work. Send as a JSON ARRAY. EXACT enum only: 'Skilling & Vocational Training' | 'Other Support (Accommodation / Travel)'. OMIT entirely if they need none (there is no 'None' value).

educationCategory.description: Highest education category (Phase-2). EXACT enum only: 'School' | 'College' | 'ITI' | 'Diploma' | 'Certification' | 'Learned Informally' | 'Other Vocational Training'.

nameOfLastRoleHeld.description: Free text; the caller's most recent job role. ONLY when experienced (workExperience 'Worked before'/'Returning after a break').

polytechnicDiploma.description: Only if educationCategory='Diploma'. Enum: 'Diploma in Mechanical' | 'Diploma in Electrical' | 'Diploma in Electronics' | 'Diploma in Civil' | 'Diploma in Computer Science' | 'Diploma in Automobile' | 'Diploma in Others'.

certificationDetails.description: Free text; only if educationCategory='Certification' or 'Learned Informally' — what certification/skill they have.

polytechnicDiplomaOther.description: Free text; only if polytechnicDiploma='Diploma in Others'.

vocationalTrainingOther.description: Free text; only if educationCategory='Other Vocational Training'.

workExperienceYearsConditional.description: Years of experience — ONLY when workExperience is 'Worked before' or 'Returning after a break'. Map the spoken answer to the NEAREST bucket. Enum: '0' | '< 1 Year' | '1 Year' | '2 Years' | '3 Years' | '3-5 Years' | '5-10 Years' | '10-15 Years' | '15+ Years'.

tools.name: apply_job
tools.description: Apply the caller to a job. Returns {results:[...], summary:{succeeded,failed}} on success; on failure an error NAMING its reason in "error":"..." - READ IT. ACTION_LIMIT_REACHED, or any message that a request already exists, means the caller ALREADY APPLIED: say so plainly, never call it a failure. Do NOT call it for a job you already know they applied to. CONSENT: never invoke this unless you have just TOLD the caller their personal details will be shared with the company - the apply question on its own is not consent, and dropping that sentence is the commonest way this goes wrong. Writing about applying does not apply: if you said you are applying you MUST invoke this tool in that same turn, never say the application went through until this tool returns a result, and never emit a stage direction like "(Silent tool call: apply_job)" - the caller hears it and nothing was applied. WHEN THIS TOOL FAILS, YOUR TURN MUST END BY ASKING WHETHER TO TELL THEM ABOUT OTHER JOBS.

job_id.description: The job's Signals item_id: a full hyphenated UUID (8-4-4-4-12), copied verbatim from the selected job in job_recommendations. Never strip the hyphens.

profile_id.description: The caller's SEEKER PROFILE item_id (a UUID). Pick the get_profile item whose item_type is "profile_1.0" AND item_domain is "seeker" - NEVER just items[0]. get_profile also returns items the caller owns as a provider (item_type "job_posting_1.0"); sending one of those as profile_id fails with SOURCE_ITEM_NOT_FOUND, which is what happened twice on call 0d63dc50. If no profile_1.0/seeker item exists the caller has NO profile: run create_profile first and use the id it returns.

duplicate_check.description: REQUIRED — you must run this check before every call. Has the caller ALREADY applied to THIS job? Look at two things: (a) has apply_job already run for this same job_id earlier in this call, with either result; and (b) does the caller context's jobs_applied already list this job — the same role at the same company, ignoring a Ltd / Limited / Pvt Ltd suffix and a shortened role name. Send 'not-applied-before' ONLY when you have looked at both and neither is true. If EITHER is true, do NOT call this tool: say the already-applied line from the instructions instead ('इस जॉब के लिए आपकी एप्लीकेशन पहले से लगी हुई है — दोबारा अप्लाई करने की ज़रूरत नहीं।'), because a call on a job whose application already exists can only fail. The one case where you may call it anyway is when you have already told the caller it is applied and they have asked you to try again regardless — then send 'caller-asked-again-anyway' and let the API decide. Never send 'not-applied-before' without actually having looked.

acting_as_user_id.description: The PROFILE OWNER's user_id (a UUID): the value of the TOP-LEVEL user_id field in the get_profile or create_profile response you received IN THIS CALL. It is NEVER equal to profile_id - profile_id comes from items[].item_id, this comes from the response's top-level user_id, and they are two different UUIDs. Before you emit this call, check that the two values differ; if they are the same you have not got a user_id and the call will fail with USER_NOT_FOUND ('acting_as_user_id does not resolve to any user') - call 5f0d3671 sent both fields as 687fd5a1... and the caller's application was lost while she was told it already existed. If you have not seen a get_profile or create_profile result in THIS call you do not have this value: knowing the caller's name or profile id from remembered context is not a user_id - call get_profile first and read it from the response.

tools.description: Update (merge new fields into) the caller's EXISTING live profile. Pass profile_id + name + age + phone ALWAYS, plus ONLY the field(s) you are persisting this turn. Merges into the item; keeps it live. Never pass a field empty.

age.description: The caller's age (the API requires it on every update — pass the known value). Send as a NUMBER, not a string.

name.description: The caller's name (the API requires it on every update — pass the known value).

role.description: Pass ONLY when persisting the job role interested in. OMIT entirely otherwise.

phone.description: The caller's number in the SAME form you sent to get_profile: 12 digits beginning with 91, digits only, no plus sign - e.g. 919876543210. tools.name: record_consent
tools.description: Record the caller's spoken consent to the TERMS (terms of use, privacy policy, holding their details) on their EXISTING profile. THE FIVE-ELEMENT TERMS DISCLOSURE IS THE ONLY TRIGGER. An apply-consent is NOT it: "shall I apply for this job" shares details with ONE employer; this records acceptance of the platform's terms. On call 9df94781 the disclosure was never spoken, only the apply question was, and this tool fired anyway - a fabricated consent record, worse than recording nothing. Cannot point to the turn in THIS call where you read the disclosure and they agreed? Do not call it. Call ONCE, silently, only when get_profile showed a consent flag false. Works on a live OR draft seeker item: against a draft it records consent and turns that item LIVE, so no second profile is needed - use it instead of create_profile for an existing-but-unconsented caller. Never after they decline. Never when get_profile came back empty (no item to record against; create_profile handles them).

age.description: The caller's age as already stored on the profile (the API requires it on every write). Send as a NUMBER, not a string.

name.description: The caller's name as already stored on the profile (the API requires it on every write). English / Latin script.

phone.description: The caller's number in the SAME form you sent to get_profile: 12 digits beginning with 91, digits only, no plus sign - e.g. 919876543210. Build it by FORMAT, not by adding: if ${contact_phone} is already 12 digits starting with 91 (outbound calls), send it UNCHANGED and never add another 91; if it is 10 digits (inbound calls), put 91 in front. A number starting 9191 is always wrong - the backend finds users by phone, so a doubled prefix silently creates a separate phantom user.

profile_id.description: The caller's seeker profile item_id (a UUID) from get_profile - the item whose item_type is "profile_1.0" and item_domain is "seeker". Use the live one if there is one, otherwise the draft you are reusing (a draft is the main case: this call turns it live). Never empty.

terms_check.description: REQUIRED — answer this before you call the tool. Did you speak the FULL five-element account-and-terms disclosure in THIS call (the account created on Blue Dots from their name and phone, the three purposes, the one-year term, managed by Ekstep Foundation, full terms readable in the app) AND did the caller then agree to THAT question? Only then is the value 'disclosure-read-and-agreed-this-call'. Otherwise the value is 'not-read' — and if it is 'not-read' you must NOT call this tool at all, because there is no consent to record. A caller agreeing to APPLY to a job is NOT agreement to the terms: the apply question shares their details with one employer, this records acceptance of the platform's terms and privacy policy. Recording a consent the caller was never asked for is a fabricated record and is worse than recording nothing.

tools.name: get_recommended_jobs
tools.description: Get jobs matched to THIS caller, ranked best-first. Call it once the caller has said they want work and get_profile returned a seeker profile: pass that profile's item_id and the backend returns the jobs closest to their stored profile, each with a score. Use this for a caller who has a profile and has NOT named a specific role - it is the personalised recommendation. If they name a role or interest instead, use get_jobs with those words. Returns message.items[]: item_id (the job_id to apply with), score, and item_state with role, jobProviderName (the company), positions, salaryMin/salaryMax when present. jobProviderLocation is masked on this instance - never speak it. Only jobs within 20 km of the caller's stored place come back. If it returns an error (ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND: the profile is too new; ANCHOR_HAS_NO_LOCATION: no stored place), call get_jobs with the caller's words instead, in the same turn. Never invent a job that is not in the result.

profile_id.description: The caller's seeker profile item_id (a UUID) from get_profile - the item whose item_type is "profile_1.0" and item_domain is "seeker". Never a job id, never a user_id.

tools.name: get_jobs
tools.description: Find jobs by what the caller said they want. Pass their role or interest as English words (e.g. "data entry operator", "electrician", "security guard", "tailoring") - translate what they said in Hindi into English before sending, and send the WORK they want, not a place. Use this when the caller names a role, asks for something different from what their profile says, or has no profile. For a caller with a profile who has not named a role, use get_recommended_jobs instead. Returns message.items[]: item_id (the job_id to apply with), score, and item_state with role, jobProviderName (the company), positions, salaryMin/salaryMax when present. jobProviderLocation is masked on this instance - never speak it. An empty items[] means we genuinely have nothing in that role: say so plainly and never invent one.

query.description: The role or kind of work the caller wants, in ENGLISH words. Translate their Hindi into English first ("डेटा एंट्री" -> "data entry operator", "बिजली का काम" -> "electrician"). Words only - no place names, no salary, no punctuation.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: Get the support services available to job seekers on this network - training and skilling centres, career counselling, interview preparation, placement assistance, government career centres, and help with things like travel or accommodation. Call this when the caller says they are NOT looking for a job right now, when jobs did not suit them, or when they mention a need a service could meet (they want training, they lack a skill or a certificate, they need help preparing for interviews, they need financial or travel help). Also worth offering AFTER a successful application. Takes no parameters. Returns items[] with item_state: organisationName, serviceDescription, costToBeneficiary, serviceAreas, and the services lists (servicesEducationalForSeekers / servicesNonEducationalForSeekers) plus who they serve (targetSeekersEducational / targetSeekersNonEducational). Match those against what the caller actually told you and offer only what fits; never invent a service or a provider that is not in the result.

tools.name: record_consent_new
tools.description: Save a NEW caller's spoken consent (terms of use, privacy policy, holding their details) the moment they say yes, when get_profile returned NO seeker item. Creates their record with the consent and a draft seeker profile. Needs the caller's name and an age they said aloud (integer, 18 or over). Never use it when get_profile returned a seeker item (use record_consent with that item_id). Returns the participant: keep the seeker item's item_id and the top-level user_id; later complete that item with update_profile and apply with it, never create_profile. An error is not a refusal: carry on with the call.

age.description: The age in years the caller SAID ALOUD this call in answer to the age question. Send as a NUMBER, not a string. Never an estimate, never an example value, never guessed: if they have not said it, ask and wait, and do not call this tool.

name.description: The caller's name: a usable ${contact_name}, or the name they said aloud this call. English / Latin script.

phone.description: The caller's number in the SAME form you sent to get_profile: 12 digits beginning with 91, digits only, no plus sign - e.g. 919876543210. Build it by FORMAT, not by adding: if ${contact_phone} is already 12 digits starting with 91 (outbound calls), send it UNCHANGED and never add another 91; if it is 10 digits (inbound calls), put 91 in front. A number starting 9191 is always wrong - the backend finds users by phone, so a doubled prefix silently creates a separate phantom user.

tools.name: get_jobs_near
tools.description: Jobs of the kind the caller asked for, near them. Use it when get_profile returned a seeker profile and the caller named a role or interest (or the profile's role is unusable). profile_id = that profile's item_id; query = the kind of work in English words, no place names. Only jobs within 20 km of the caller's stored place come back. If it returns an error (ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND or ANCHOR_HAS_NO_LOCATION), call get_jobs with the same query instead, in the same turn. Returns message.items[] like get_recommended_jobs. Never invent a job that is not in the result.

query.description: The kind of work the caller asked for, in English words ("data entry operator", "electrician"). No place name, no salary, no punctuation. Never empty.

profile_id.description: The caller's seeker profile item_id (a UUID) from get_profile - the item whose item_type is "profile_1.0" and item_domain is "seeker". Never a job id, never a user_id.
